summary: Describes Asynchronous Layered Coding, a massively scalable, reliable content delivery protocol. It combines the Layered Coding Transport building block, multiple-rate congestion control and forward error correction to deliver content to an unlimited number of receivers at once. This is an experimental protocol, replaced by RFC 5775.

eli5.summary: Imagine a radio tower sending a file to millions of listeners, with extra repair data so nobody has to ask for a resend. This is an experimental design for that. It was replaced by RFC 5775.

questions: how does alc scale to millions of receivers
what is layered coding in multicast
subtitle: Massive-scale reliable content delivery using layered coding and multicast.

tldr.problem: Broadcasting files to millions of receivers without feedback requires both reliability (to recover from lost packets) and congestion control (to share network fairly).
tldr.mechanism: ALC combines forward error correction to add redundant repair data, layered coding transport to manage session metadata, and multi-rate congestion control where each receiver independently adjusts its reception rate by joining or leaving multicast channels.
tldr.outcome: A single sender can transmit to an unlimited number of concurrent receivers at no additional load, with each receiver using only its fair share of available bandwidth. This was experimental; RFC 5775 replaced it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
ALC is a protocol for massively scalable reliable content delivery designed for IP multicast. It enables a single sender to transmit content to an unlimited number of receivers at the same time, with each receiver receiving at the maximum fair bandwidth available on its path to the sender.

Unlike unicast protocols such as TCP where the sender must maintain connection state for each receiver, ALC is completely stateless at the sender. All receivers that want the same content simply join the same multicast group and listen. If a receiver's network link loses some packets, ALC uses forward error correction to recover the missing data without requiring the receiver to ask for a retransmission.
sections.eli5: ALC lets one server send the same file to a million people at once, like a radio broadcast. Each person can tune in whenever they want, adjust their signal quality, and fix any broken parts using spare data.

sections.title: Architecture and Building Blocks
sections.content:
ALC combines three core building blocks:

Layered Coding Transport (LCT) carries session management information in the packet header, including a Transport Session ID (TSI) to identify the session, and optionally a Transport Object ID (TOI) when multiple files are sent in one session.

Forward Error Correction (FEC) transforms each object into a stream of encoding symbols. The sender generates more symbols than the original data requires, so receivers can recover the entire object once they collect enough symbols, without needing retransmission.

Multiple-rate congestion control lets each receiver independently adjust its reception rate. Rather than the sender controlling a single rate for everyone, the receiver joins multiple multicast channels at different transmission rates. By joining fewer channels when congested and more channels when bandwidth is available, each receiver fairly uses network resources.
sections.eli5: Three pieces work together: a header that marks which file this packet belongs to, extra data that lets you rebuild missing packets, and the ability for each receiver to say 'I can only handle slow data right now, so I'll skip the high-speed channel.'

sections.title: Packet Format
sections.content:
An ALC packet carries a UDP header, followed by an LCT header with congestion control information, followed by an FEC Payload ID identifying which source block and encoding symbol the payload contains, and finally the encoded data itself.

The LCT header includes several optional fields: a Source Block Number and Encoding Symbol ID that index into the encoding symbols for an object; a Sender Current Time to communicate elapsed session time; and an Expected Residual Time telling receivers how much longer the sender will transmit this object. Flags indicate whether the session or the current object is about to close.

Header Extensions provide a way to add optional fields such as packet authentication or per-object FEC transmission information without changing the version number.
sections.eli5: Each packet is like a labeled package: the address label (LCT header) says which file and which piece of that file, the delivery receipt marks how long the broadcast will last, and the package itself holds encoded data.

sections.title: Sender and Receiver Operation
sections.content:
The sender generates ALC packets from objects to be delivered, fills in the LCT header fields, and sends packets to the multicast channels at rates determined by the congestion control building block. The sender must publish a Session Description that receivers need before joining, containing the congestion control scheme, sender IP address, multicast channels, session ID, and FEC scheme to use. The sender also provides FEC Object Transmission Information describing how each object is encoded.

The receiver first obtains a Session Description to learn how to join the session. Upon receiving each packet, it verifies the header is valid, checks that the TSI matches an expected session, adjusts its reception rate using congestion control, verifies the TOI if multiple objects are in the session, and then uses the FEC Payload ID to accumulate encoding symbols and reconstruct the object.
sections.eli5: The sender prepares everything receivers need to know (the Session Description) and then continuously sends encoded packets. Each receiver listens, adjusts how many channels it follows based on network conditions, and pieces together the original file.

sections.title: Status and Security
sections.content:
This RFC is an experimental protocol instantiation as per RFC 3048. ALC is designed to eventually become an Internet Standard pending adequate congestion control, but was superseded by RFC 5775.

ALC relies on the security properties of its building blocks. Packet authentication is recommended via Header Extensions to prevent unauthorized senders from injecting packets into a session. If authentication is used, receivers SHOULD check it immediately upon receipt before performing congestion control actions, though some schemes like TESLA may require delayed verification.
sections.eli5: This was an experiment that worked well but got improved in later versions. The main security concern is making sure packets really come from the sender you expect, using authentication codes.
